name: A-prime why key (EU / UK / U.S. regulator stage), labelled by a separate AI reviewer
annotator: Separate AI reviewer (Claude, in its own session), NOT a pharmacist; it did not read the system outputs
method: Read only set1a_questions.json from the project folder; no other project files, outputs, logs or keys opened.

US: downloaded all 14 FDA AEMS quarterly "New Safety Information or Potential Signals of Serious Risks" pages (Jan-Mar 2023 through Apr-Jun 2026, links from the AEMS index page) with a browser User-Agent, parsed every table row (295 rows), keyword-matched drug, brand, class and reaction terms per question, matched the reaction by meaning, and took the label from the status column.
US: scanned the FDA Drug Safety Communications index for each drug; fetched the clozapine REMS DSC; searched fda.gov for CBER safety communications on Ixchiq and for valproate paternal exposure.

UK: listed all 869 Drug Safety Update documents via the gov.uk search API (filter_format=drug_safety_update), fetched each body through the gov.uk content API, and full-text searched drug/brand/class names (this includes the monthly Letters and medicine recalls round-ups).
UK: fetched all 19 MHRA Safety Roundups (Mar 2025-Sep 2026) and full-text searched them the same way, plus reaction keywords.
UK: ran gov.uk search API queries per question (drug alone and drug+reaction), with and without filter_format, and reviewed MHRA items dated 2025-2026.
EU: kept "concluded" for all rows by construction; looked at EMA PRAC extracts only for R183 (erdafitinib growth accelerated / epiphysiolysis) and R185 (Ixchiq aseptic meningitis).
Confidence: high = exact drug+reaction entry, or a thorough negative search; medium = class/partial-product or meaning-based match; low = related but not identical reaction.
